I’m checking whether narrowly gated examples or compact label summaries have enough repeat structure to justify memory, instead of assuming more examples will help.

"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command "@'
import json,re,collections,itertools
rows=[json.loads(s) for s in open('anonymous_traces.jsonl',encoding='utf-8') if s.strip()]
by_input={r['input']:r for r in rows}
items=list(by_input.values())
def parts(s):
 m=re.search(r'(?is)\\bContext\\s*:\\s*(.*?)\\bInput\\s*:\\s*(.*?)(?:\\bAnswer\\s*:|"'$)'"',s)
 return (re.sub(r'\\s+',' ',m.group(1)).strip().casefold(),m.group(2).strip()) if m else ('',s.strip())
def tok(s): return set(re.findall(r'[a-z]+|\\d+|["'^'"\\w\\s]',s.casefold()))
def jac(a,b): return len(a&b)/len(a|b) if a|b else 0
cats=collections.defaultdict(list); targets=collections.Counter()
for r in items:
 c,x=parts(r['input']); cats[c].append(r); targets[r['ground_truth']]+=1
print('unique inputs',len(items),'unique targets',len(targets),'duplicate targets',sum(n>1 for n in targets.values()))
print('context buckets',[(c,len(rs),len(set(x['ground_truth'] for x in rs))) for c,rs in sorted(cats.items())])
vals=[]
for r in items:
 c,x=parts(r['input']); same=[]; allx=[]
 for o in items:
  if o is r: continue
  oc,ox=parts(o['input']); sc=jac(tok(x),tok(ox)); allx.append((sc,oc==c))
  if oc==c: same.append(sc)
 vals.append((max(same,default=0),max((v for v,_ in allx),default=0),len(same)))
print('same-context nearest similarity quantiles', sorted(v[0] for v in vals))
print('all nearest similarity quantiles', sorted(v[1] for v in vals))
print('same-context peer counts',collections.Counter(v[2] for v in vals))
print('target component count',collections.Counter(1+r['ground_truth'].count('.') for r in items))
print('target lengths quantiles',sorted(len(r['ground_truth']) for r in items))
print('input lengths quantiles',sorted(len(r['input']) for r in items))
'@ | python -"
